Plot joint residuals of the fits to indices of abundance

Source: R/plot_joint_residuals.R
plot_joint_residuals.Rd

Plot the residuals of the fits to all indices over time with a loess smoother and a fit statistic, as in JABBA (jbplot_residuals() and jbplot_stdresiduals()) and ss3diags (SSplotJABBAres()). A trend in the smoother shows a pattern in the residuals; a large statistic shows a poor fit.

plot_joint_residuals(
  dat,
  fleet = NULL,
  module = NULL,
  scaled = FALSE,
  overlay = TRUE,
  show_stat = TRUE,
  ncol = NULL,
  interactive = TRUE,
  make_rda = FALSE,
  figures_dir = getwd()
)

Arguments

dat

A tibble from convert_output() with labels "index_observed" and "index_predicted".

fleet

Character vector. Fleet(s) to plot. Default: NULL (all fleets)

module

Character vector. (Optional) Module name found in dat$module_name. If selecting >1 module, place them in a vector like c("module1", "module2").

Default: NULL

If the interactive and >1 module_name is found, user will select the module_name in the console. @seealso filter_data()

scaled

Logical. TRUE/FALSE; plot standardized residuals (log residuals divided by their standard error) instead of log residuals.

Default: FALSE

overlay

Logical. TRUE/FALSE; plot all indices on one panel, with a boxplot of the residuals in each year. FALSE plots each index on its own panel.

Default: TRUE

show_stat

Logical. TRUE/FALSE; show the fit statistic in the top right corner of each panel: the root mean square error (RMSE) of log residuals, or the standard deviation of normalized residuals (SDNR) of scaled residuals. When overlay = TRUE, the statistic of each index is also shown in the legend.

Default: TRUE

ncol

Number. Number of columns of panels when overlay = FALSE.

Default: NULL

interactive

Logical. TRUE/FALSE; indicate whether the environment is interactive.

Default: FALSE

make_rda

Logical. TRUE/FALSE; indicate whether to save the object and make an automated caption and alternative text in the form of an rda object. If TRUE, the rda will be exported to the folder indicated in the argument "figures_dir".

Default: FALSE.

figures_dir

Path. Path to the "figures" folder.

Default: getwd()

The folder is created within the path if it does not exist.

Value

A ggplot2 object.

Details

Log residuals are \(r = \log(o) - \log(p)\) for observed \(o\) and predicted \(p\), as in plot_runs_test(); scaled residuals are \(z = r / s\) for the log-scale standard error \(s\) of the observation. The RMSE is \(100 \sqrt{\overline{r^2}}\) percent. The SDNR is \(\sqrt{\sum z^2 / (n - 1)}\), shown with its critical value \(\sqrt{\chi^2_{0.95, n - 1} / (n - 1)}\); an SDNR above the critical value suggests the standard errors are too small (Francis 2011).

The smoother is a loess regression (span 0.75) of the mean residual of each year on year, for all indices together or for each index on its own panel. It is not drawn for fewer than five years of residuals, or when the years are too sparse for a stable fit; a message names the indices without one.

Observations are treated as in plot_runs_test(): a fleet observed in more than one area, season, subseason, month, or sex becomes separate series, and observations without a positive observed and predicted value are reported in a message. Scaled residuals also need a standard error; observations without one are reported in a message.

References

Francis, R.I.C.C. 2011. Data weighting in statistical fisheries stock assessment models. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 68: 1124-1138.

See also

plot_runs_test(), plot_index(), convert_output()

Examples

plot_joint_residuals(stockplotr::example_data, interactive = FALSE)

plot_joint_residuals(
  stockplotr::example_data,
  scaled = TRUE,
  overlay = FALSE,
  interactive = FALSE
)
